title: rbxplace.toml
description: Environment map shared by every rbx subcommand: env name to universe id, the places under it, and the project owner. See docs/env.md.

codegen.description: Codegen output path for `rbx env gen-module`.

owner.description: Default owner for every env. Per-env `[<env>.owner]` overrides win when set. See `PlacesFile::resolve_owner`.

Environment.description:
One `[<env>]` table: a named environment pointing at one universe.

`universe_id` is required; everything else is optional. An unrecognised key is kept rather than rejected, and reported on stderr instead.

codegen.description:
Whether game code should see this env (default: `true`).

`false` marks an env that exists for tooling only: a universe you upload to from CI and never ship. It stays a normal env everywhere else: `--env` resolves it, `--env all` includes it, `list` and `get` report it. It is only kept out of the generated modules, so adding one does not widen the `EnvironmentType` union and force game code to acknowledge an env it never runs in.

The trade, and it is real: nothing then maps that universe back to an env at runtime. Boot the game there and code that resolves its env from `game.GameId` will not find one. Correct for a universe that only ever receives uploads, wrong for one that runs gameplay.

confirm.description: Prompt before a write to this env: `upload`, `sync`, `rollback`, `promote`. Defaults to `false`.

env.description:
What game code matches on, when it should differ from the section name.

A rename, not an alias: two envs resolving to the same name is an error, not two spellings of one env.

owner.description: Per-env owner override. When unset, callers fall back to the top-level `[owner]` (see `PlacesFile::resolve_owner`).

places.description: Per-place id map. Tools that operate at universe scope (rbx shop, rbx meta universe-level fields) leave this empty; tools that need a place id (rbx place, rbx meta place-level fields) read it.

universe_id.description: The universe this env targets. Required.

Owner.description: Who owns the project. Tools without their own owner field fall back to this one.

OwnerType.description: Whether a project is owned by a user account or by a group.

PlacesCodegen.description:
Reserved `[codegen]` block: where `rbx env gen-module` writes its module.

The path lives here rather than only in `--out` so the hook, the CI job and the developer cannot disagree about it: a `--check` pointed at a path nobody generates passes green while verifying nothing.

output.description: Output file path. The format follows the extension: `.lua`, `.luau`, `.json` or `.ts`.
